headline: Reflection AI unveils open-weight model Beam to rival Chinese labs
body: Reflection AI unveiled Beam on Oct 5, a text-only mixture-of-experts model with 501 billion parameters, 23 billion of them active, pretrained on 23.8 trillion tokens with a 1 million token context window. The company says Beam matches Z.ai's GLM-5.2 on reasoning benchmarks using "3-4x less inference compute," and has raised roughly $4.7 billion from backers including Nvidia, Sequoia Capital and Lightspeed Venture Partners, according to PitchBook data reported by TechCrunch.
note: A Western open-weight model claiming Chinese-rival performance at a fraction of the compute cost could lower the price of running frontier-grade AI in-house, a real alternative for banks and insurers weighing proprietary deployments against API access to closed models.

evidence.text: Reflection debuts Beam, an open-weight AI model to rival Chinese models at lower compute cost
Reflection AI is officially unveiling Beam, its first frontier, open-weight AI model.

The two-year-old, Brooklyn-based startup claims Beam matches the performance of leading Chinese open models on advanced reasoning benchmarks at dramatically lower costs, a claim that could heat up the race to build a Western answer to DeepSeek, Qwen, and Z.ai.

The company shared new details in a lengthy blog post Monday , which described Beam as a text-only mixture-of-experts model trained on high-compute reinforcement learning to be effective at reasoning, coding, and agentic tasks at “a fraction of the token cost and inference time compute” of rivals.
Beam is a 501-billion-parameter model with 23 billion active parameters.
It was pretrained on 23.8 trillion tokens and has a 1 million token context window.

Reflection’s performance claims haven’t been independently verified, but on advanced reasoning benchmarks, the company says Beam scores on par with Z.ai’s GLM-5.2 and outperforms today’s leading Western open models while using “3-4x less inference compute.”

Reflection was founded in 2024 by two former Google DeepMind researchers and has raised roughly $4.7 billion from backers, including Nvidia, Sequoia Capital, and Lightspeed Venture Partners, per PitchBook.
